7. Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on- record, appearing for the appellant, reiterated the submissions on which leave was granted. 

 11. The above finding given by the learned Judge of the single Bench is fundamentally a question of fact. The finding is very specific and has been given with reference to the materials available in the record of the pre-emption miscellaneous case and also the order dated 12-9-1996 passed therein. Mr. Nawab Ali could not show from the records that the finding of the learned Judge of the single Bench as quoted hereinbefore is contrary to the records of the case or the order dated 12-9-1996 passed in the preemption miscellaneous case and based on misreading of the said order. Therefore, the finding of the learned Assistant Judge that since on behalf of the pre-emptee-petitioners prayer for time for filing written objection was made, so it was not believable that the pre-emptee-petitioners had no knowledge of the pre-emption miscellaneous case does not hold good.
